narrative.overview: One panel, one pattern: everything is a tile. Home is a grid of the tools the user switched on; a tool opens into a dashboard of tiles. The panel is quiet and monochrome, and color appears only when it carries a meaning: amber for paused or caution, blue for the user's control, green for healthy. Dark-first but designed twice, with light as its own set of values.
keyCharacteristics: A single container, the tile (16 pt continuous corner, 1 pt hairline), builds every view.
Near-black ground with slightly lifted tiles in dark; white tiles on pale gray in light.
Three accents, each with one meaning; everything else is neutral.
System font only; values at 24 pt semibold with tabular digits, everything else 11 to 17 pt.
Flat: no shadows on any tile or control; depth is tonal plus hairline.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Each accent means one thing: amber is paused or over a limit, blue is the user's control, green is healthy. Never use an accent as decoration.

rules.name: The Paired Appearance Rule
rules.body: Every color role has an explicit light and dark value. Do not derive one by inverting the other.

rules.name: The Tinted Text Rule
rules.body: Accent text on a tile uses the accent's own text value, hand-checked to at least 5.4:1 in both appearances. Do not put a bar-fill value on text.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number that can change while the panel is open uses tabular digits so the layout does not jitter.

rules.name: The Small Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Nothing but the header title and values is above 15 pt; the panel is not a place for display type.

rules.name: The Flat Tile Rule
rules.body: Tiles never get shadows. State is shown by fill, outline color, or dash, not by lift.

dos: Do build every new view from Tile, in whole columns (1, 2, or 3) with a 12 pt gap.
Do give every new color a light and a dark value and check text at 4.5:1 or better on its tile.
Do use native SF Symbols, native menus, and native keyboard behavior.
Do honor Reduce Motion: the limit change animates with a 0.2 s spring, and snaps when Reduce Motion is on.
Do give each tile an accessibility label that states the value and its context, and hide decorative bars and charts from VoiceOver.
Do use the production switch: native Toggle with tint. The drawn PreviewSwitchStyle is a harness stand-in.
donts: Don't add shadows, gradients, or glow to tiles or controls.
Don't use an accent for decoration, or add a fourth accent.
Don't use a big ring with a percentage, three identical stat cards, or sparklines that replace readable data.
Don't use a non-system font for UI; run a font licensing check before any custom face.
Don't assume a vibrancy material: the panel is a solid Ground fill; a material is an optional production decision.
Don't copy another app's name, icons, or copy; the working title must not ship as a public name.
